claims.text: The as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy has a single-phase hexagonal structure.
The as-deposited alloy exhibits a sharp magnetocaloric response.
The as-deposited alloy exhibits strong hysteresis during low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Controlled low-temperature annealing refines the alloy microstructure.
Controlled low-temperature annealing makes the microstructure more uniform.
Annealing can alter grain size, grain-boundary density, or nanoscale precipitates.
The annealed microstructure has a more uniform distribution of transformation nucleation sites.
The distribution of nucleation sites governs phase-transformation dynamics.
Annealing-induced microstructural modifications lower local energy barriers for the first-order magnetostructural transition.
Lower local transformation barriers produce a smoother and more gradual magnetostructural transformation.
A smoother transformation reduces hysteretic losses during low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
The annealed alloy preserves a strong or effective magnetocaloric response.
Annealed samples will have a broader and less abrupt entropy-change profile than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will exhibit less hysteresis than the as-deposited baseline under low-applied-field cycles.
The predictions apply only while the alloy retains its single-phase hexagonal structure.
The predictions apply only under processing conditions that avoid excessive phase change and loss of mechanical stability.
The predicted effects are confined to the temperature range of the magnetostructural transition.
